guides.name: BPC-157
guides.aka: Body Protection Compound-157, PL 14736, PL-10, Bepecin
guides.dopingStatus: Prohibited by WADA under Category S0 (Non-approved substances)
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Unregistered pharmaceutical; research & educational chemical only under DDA Nepal guidelines.

facts.label: Origin
facts.text: Synthesized 15-amino acid sequence derived from human gastric juice protein.

facts.label: Primary Research Target
facts.text: Angiogenesis (blood vessel formation via VEGF-A pathways), tendon-to-bone junction repair, and gastrointestinal mucosal healing.

facts.label: Human Clinical Status
facts.text: Limited published Phase 1 human trials for inflammatory bowel disease; most preclinical data from rodent models.

facts.label: Athletic Doping
facts.text: Strictly prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) at all times (in and out of competition).

sources.title: Sikiric et al., Brain-gut axis and BPC-157 in tissue repair (PubMed 27847966)
Chang et al., The promoting effect of pentadecapeptide BPC 157 on tendon healing (PubMed 21030672)

guides.name: TB-500 (Thymosin Beta-4)
guides.dopingStatus: Prohibited by WADA under Category S2 (Peptide hormones & growth factors)
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Unregistered in Nepal. Sourced from partner laboratory for research.

facts.label: Mechanism
facts.text: Upregulates cellular actin sequestration, accelerating cell migration to wound sites and reducing fibrosis.

facts.label: Synergy with BPC-157
facts.text: While BPC-157 promotes localized angiogenesis, TB-500 acts systemically on cellular actin and tissue flexibility.

facts.label: Doping Classification
facts.text: Banned in human and equine competitive sports.

sources.title: Goldstein et al., Thymosin beta 4: a key player in tissue repair (PubMed 16040810)
Philp et al., Thymosin beta4 promotes angiogenesis and wound healing (PubMed 14612450)

guides.name: Semaglutide
guides.dopingStatus: Not prohibited by WADA; permitted in sports subject to medical prescription.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Approved by US FDA and European EMA; imported under specialized medical protocols in Nepal.

facts.label: Class
facts.text: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist with a C18 fatty diacid chain.

facts.label: Mechanism
facts.text: Stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, inhibits glucagon, delays gastric emptying, and reduces central appetite in the hypothalamus.

facts.label: Clinical Proof
facts.text: Extensive randomized Phase 3 STEP clinical trials demonstrating 15% average total body weight loss over 68 weeks.

facts.label: Side Effects
facts.text: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, and rare risk of pancreatitis or biliary disease.

sources.title: Wilding et al., STEP 1 Trial of Once-Weekly Semaglutide (NEJM 2021; 384:989-1002)

guides.name: Tirzepatide
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: FDA approved; registered research and imported clinical compound.

facts.label: Class
facts.text: Dual GIP (Glucose-dependent Insulinotropic Polypeptide) and GLP-1 receptor agonist.

facts.label: Efficacy
facts.text: SURMOUNT-1 Phase 3 trials demonstrated up to 20.9% mean body weight reduction, outperforming GLP-1 mono-agonists.

facts.label: Metabolic Action
facts.text: Improves insulin sensitivity, suppresses glucagon, and optimizes lipid metabolism.

sources.title: Jastreboff et al., Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity (NEJM 2022; 387:205-216)

guides.name: Retatrutide
guides.dopingStatus: Not specifically listed; monitored under non-approved performance agents.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Experimental research only. Sourced from partner laboratory for verified testing.

facts.label: Mechanism
facts.text: Triple agonist engaging GLP-1, GIP, and Glucagon receptors simultaneously.

facts.label: Phase 2 Trials
facts.text: Published in NEJM 2023 with unprecedented weight reduction reaching up to 24.2% at 48 weeks.

facts.label: Thermogenic Action
facts.text: Glucagon receptor activation elevates resting energy expenditure and hepatic fat oxidation.

sources.title: Rosenstock et al., Triple–Hormone-Receptor Agonist Retatrutide (NEJM 2023; 389:514-526)

guides.name: GHK-Cu
guides.dopingStatus: Permitted. Naturally occurring human plasma tripeptide.

facts.label: Endogenous Role
facts.text: Discovered by Dr. Loren Pickart in 1973; naturally declines with age from 200 ng/ml at age 20 to 80 ng/ml at age 60.

facts.label: Gene Expression
facts.text: Regulates over 4,000 human genes, upregulating collagen I, III, decorin, and metalloproteinases.

facts.label: Skin & Follicle
facts.text: Broadly researched for skin remodeling, dermal thickness, and hair follicle enlargement.

sources.title: Pickart & Margolina, Regenerative and Protective Actions of the GHK-Cu Peptide (PubMed 30166113)

quiz.statement: BPC-157 is an FDA-approved medicine for muscle and joint injuries.
quiz.explanation: BPC-157 is not FDA-approved for human medicine. It remains an experimental research peptide. While pre-clinical animal studies are promising, human clinical trial data is limited.
quiz.reference: FDA 503A Bulks List Guidance & Pre-clinical Review

quiz.statement: BPC-157 and TB-500 are banned in all WADA-tested sports.
quiz.explanation: The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) explicitly prohibits BPC-157 under Category S0 (Unapproved Substances) and TB-500 under Category S2. Athletes using them risk multi-year suspensions.

quiz.statement: Oral BPC-157 capsules are completely destroyed by stomach acid.
quiz.explanation: Unlike many fragile proteins, BPC-157 is originally derived from human gastric juice and has notable stability in gastric acid (especially in arginate or enteric formulations), making oral administration viable for GI research.
quiz.reference: Sikiric et al., Current Pharmaceutical Design, 2011

quiz.statement: Semaglutide and Tirzepatide work on the exact same single hormone pathway.
quiz.explanation: Semaglutide targets only the GLP-1 receptor. Tirzepatide is a 'twincretin' that targets both GLP-1 and GIP receptors, which clinical trials showed produces greater average weight and glycemic improvements.

quiz.statement: Independent third-party HPLC & Mass Spectrometry testing is essential to confirm peptide purity.
quiz.explanation: Peptides can degrade or carry synthesis byproducts. Only third-party HPLC (verifying purity percentage) and Mass Spec (verifying molecular weight) confirm what is actually inside the vial.
quiz.reference: Analytical Methods Committee, Royal Society of Chemistry
